high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Conducts Asset and Income Verification Lottery for Agencies and Units in 2026
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) conducted a public lottery to select agencies for asset and income verification in 2026, demonstrating transparency in anti-corruption efforts within the banking sector. SBV Chief Inspector Lai Huu Phuoc presided over the ceremony, emphasizing compliance with Party and State regulations on asset and income control. This systematic verification process is crucial for maintaining integrity in Vietnam's monetary policy implementation and banking supervision. For FX and bond markets, this reinforces institutional credibility and regulatory oversight, which are key factors international investors consider when assessing Vietnamese assets. The transparent approach to internal governance supports confidence in SBV's policy-making processes and regulatory framework.

high.title: Former Deputy Governor Dao Minh Tu Appointed as Vice Chairman and Secretary-General of Vietnam Banking Association Term VIII
high.summary: Former SBV Standing Deputy Governor Dao Minh Tu was elected Vice Chairman and Secretary-General of the Vietnam Banking Association for the 2026-2031 term. Tu, who served as SBV Deputy Governor from 2012 and was reappointed in 2017 and 2022, brings extensive monetary policy experience to the banking industry association. His appointment signals continuity in banking sector leadership and policy direction. For VND traders and bond investors, this represents institutional stability and suggests continued coordination between regulatory authorities and the banking industry. Tu's deep experience in monetary policy formulation could facilitate smoother implementation of banking reforms and financial market development initiatives.

high.title: Good News for Banks: SBV Officially Relaxes LDR Ratio, Vietcombank, BIDV and VietinBank Can Lend Additional Tens of Thousands of Billions
high.summary: The SBV issued Circular 08/2026 on May 15, modifying the calculation of State Treasury deposits in the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR), effectively relaxing credit growth constraints for banks. Under the new regulation, 20% of State Treasury time deposits can now be included in the LDR denominator, while non-term deposits remain fully excluded. This change particularly benefits large state-owned banks like Vietcombank, BIDV, and VietinBank, which hold substantial State Treasury deposits. The relaxation could unlock tens of trillions of VND in additional lending capacity, potentially boosting credit growth and economic activity. For VND/USD markets, increased credit expansion may support domestic demand but could also create inflationary pressures. Bond markets should monitor whether this leads to increased government bond issuance or changes in yield curves as liquidity conditions ease.

high.title: One Bank Approved by SBV to Increase Charter Capital by Over 6,000 Billion VND
high.summary: The SBV approved SeABank's charter capital increase of up to 6.238 trillion VND, comprising 5.838 trillion VND through dividend payment shares and 400 billion VND through employee stock options. This brings SeABank's total charter capital to 34.688 trillion VND, significantly strengthening its capital adequacy ratios under Basel III standards. The capital injection enhances SeABank's lending capacity and competitive position in the banking sector. For the VND and Vietnamese banking sector, this represents continued capitalization efforts by mid-tier banks to meet international standards. Stronger bank capital ratios support financial stability and could influence SBV's monetary policy flexibility. Bond investors should note the potential for increased competition in the lending market as well-capitalized banks expand their loan portfolios.

medium.title: Foreign Investors Sell Over 1,000 Billion VND of One Stock in Week of May 11-15
medium.summary: VN-Index closed the week at 1,921.6 points (+0.33%) near historical highs, but foreign investors sold a net 3.905 trillion VND across all markets during May 11-15. VHM was the most heavily sold stock with approximately 1.075 trillion VND in net selling. The sustained foreign selling pressure indicates cautious sentiment despite market resilience near record levels.

medium.title: VPBank Executive Successfully Purchases 30 Million VPB Shares as Registered
medium.summary: VPBank Board member Pham Thi Nhung purchased 30 million VPB shares from May 8-13, 2026, increasing her stake from 0.58% to 0.96%. The transaction cost approximately 838.5 billion VND at prevailing market prices. Additionally, VPBank repurchased its entire VPB12501 bond series two years ahead of maturity, demonstrating strong liquidity management.

medium.title: Many Major US, Chinese, Japanese Banks Want to Establish Subsidiaries at HCMC International Financial Center
medium.summary: Following the launch of Vietnam International Financial Center in HCMC (VIFC-HCMC) in February 2026, numerous domestic and international banks are registering to establish subsidiaries. Seven Vietnamese banks have already approved establishing 100% owned subsidiaries at VIFC. The center awaits final operational regulations approval but has established crucial legal frameworks through National Assembly Resolution 222/2025.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Expert Identifies Three Catalysts That Could Open New Cycle for Vietnamese Stocks
medium.summary: Dragon Capital identifies three structural drivers for Vietnamese equities: market upgrade (FTSE Emerging Market inclusion and potential MSCI EM entry within 2-3 years), industrial transformation, and demographic dividend. MSCI inclusion could bring $3-4 billion in passive inflows, representing significant capital flow support for Vietnamese markets.

medium.title: Gold Prices SJC, Plain Gold Ring Evening May 16
medium.summary: Gold prices remained flat during May 16 afternoon session but continued declining from previous day's close. SJC gold bars traded at 160.5-163.5 million VND/tael across major dealers, with buying prices down 500,000 VND/tael and selling prices down 1.5 million VND/tael from previous session.
